methodology.method_family: institutional implementation report and organizational case study
methodology.study_design: single-center prospective governance implementation with retrospective review of existing models
methodology.sample_description: Memorial Sloan Kettering Comprehensive Cancer Center AI Governance Committee one-year program covering clinical, operations, and research AI
methodology.sample_size: 26 AI models (including large language models), 2 ambient AI pilots, retrospective review of 33 nomograms
methodology.technology_context: Responsible AI governance across generative AI, ambient AI, intelligent automation, traditional AI/ML/NLP in oncology clinical, operations, and research programs

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article reports a concrete Responsible AI governance model in a regulated oncology setting and explicitly registers and monitors AI models including LLMs, ambient AI pilots, risk assessment, and lifecycle tools. It strongly supports governance, risk, and compliance themes in healthcare but the provided text does not center conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or dialogue-specific guardrails; ambient AI is mentioned without conversational governance detail.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Confirm whether ambient AI pilots and LLM use cases involve conversational interfaces and whether later sections add dialogue-specific governance, observability, or human oversight mechanisms not present in the supplied excerpts.

appraisal.notes: Descriptive single-institution implementation report with useful governance artifacts and counts, but limited generalizability beyond oncology and no rigorous comparative or experimental design evident in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are internally coherent and grounded in a one-year institutional program with named tools and inventories, but evidence is from one cancer center, largely descriptive, and weakly aligned to conversational LLM governance specifically.

coding.theme: Institutional Responsible AI governance in oncology
coding.subtheme: Governance tools and lifecycle management for diverse AI including LLMs
rq_alignment: governance and accountability in regulated domains

synthesis.main_claim: A Comprehensive Cancer Center implemented and reported a Responsible AI governance model that registered, evaluated, and monitored 26 AI models including LLMs, 2 ambient AI pilots, and 33 nomograms, and shared reusable governance tools and case studies.
synthesis.contribution: Provides one of the first published oncology-specific RAI governance reports at scale, including program structure, risk assessment, lifecycle management, and operational inventories for LLM and non-LLM models in clinical, operations, and research domains.
synthesis.limitations: Single-institution descriptive report; oncology-specific context may limit transferability; few rigorous LLM studies in cancer care noted; open research questions remain; conversational or dialogue-system governance not substantively addressed in supplied text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for institutional AI governance, registration, monitoring, and risk tooling in regulated healthcare where LLMs are part of a broader AI portfolio; not as central evidence for conversational governance unless full text confirms ambient/conversational use-case governance.
